subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add public phase, stagger, or prime-cadence controls for cron `every` schedules, and if so which contract should become canonical?
rationale: The remaining request is a public scheduling/config/API decision with persisted-state and upgrade implications, and repository policy says this should not be chosen by an autonomous bug-fix lane.

options.title: Design narrow every phase/stagger contract
options.body: Add one explicit `every` phase or stagger contract across schema, CLI, protocol, persistence, docs, status output, and upgrade tests before implementing prime cadence.

options.title: Keep every fixed
options.body: Preserve current fixed anchored `every` semantics and treat heartbeat phase plus cron-expression stagger as the supported anti-herd behavior.

options.title: Adopt broader prime mode
options.body: Add prime cadence transforms plus deterministic phase controls for heartbeat and cron, with explicit compatibility, migration, and observability requirements.

recommendation.title: Design narrow every phase/stagger contract
recommendation.body: Add one explicit `every` phase or stagger contract across schema, CLI, protocol, persistence, docs, status output, and upgrade tests before implementing prime cadence.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest merged history on cron stagger semantics and schedule contract boundaries.
